 Order

The petitioners have challenged the registration of First Information Report against them in Crime No.193/2021 by respondent No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC, which is pending consideration before the XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bengaluru City.

XXX Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate,
Bengaluru City
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The respondent No.2 informed respondent No.1 about the commission of cognizable offences by the petitioners.

She claimed that she was given in marriage to petitioner No.1 and within 15 days thereafter, the petitioners abused her claiming that she was obese and that her parents had cheated Mr Mirza Haroon Baig vs State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60408745/
2 them by marrying her off to petitioner No.1.

entities.text: Mirza Haroon Baig vs State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: They had allegedly threatened to divorce her.
She claimed that she was sent back to her parents house within one month from the date of the marriage.
She alleged that even after three months, neither her husband nor her in-laws took her back.
Thereafter, on 08.08.2021, there was a panchayath at Gulbarga.
On 09.08.2021, respondent No.2 accompanied with petitioner Nos.1 to 3, went back to her matrimonial home.
However, she was asked to stay in the ground floor in a room but was locked up there.
She alleged that the petitioners had reprimanded her that she should eat what is given to her so that she can reduce her weight.
She also alleged that petitioner No.1 disclosed that his parents did not like her and warned her to live as per their instructions, failing which, she would be divorced.
She claimed that she was day-in and day-out harassed by the petitioners and also she was threatened of her life.

She alleged that on NC: 2023:KHC:41424 16.09.2021, she was again forced to go back to her parents house and as petitioner No.1 assaulted her on 18.09.2021, she lodged a complaint before the concerned police station by calling the emergency services.
She claimed that the jurisdictional police arrived at the spot and informed her to secure her parents and to lodge a complaint before the jurisdictional police.
She alleged that she left ten tolas of gold, her dresses and other articles at her matrimonial home and lodged a complaint on 17.09.2021.

She therefore, prayed respondent No.1 to initiate suitable action against the petitioners, consequent to which, a case in Crime No.193/2021 was registered for the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC.
3. The petitioners being aggrieved by the registration of First Information Report against them have filed this petition.
4. The learned counsel for the petitioners contended that the allegations contained in the complaint are all false and far from truth.
He contends that respondent No.1 did not conduct preliminary enquiry before registering a case against the petitioners.
In this regard, he relied upon the judgment of NC: 2023:KHC:41424 the Hon'ble Apex Court in Lalitha Kumari vs. government of Uttar Pradesh and others [AIR 2014 SC 187].

entities.text: Lalitha Kumari vs. government of Uttar Pradesh and others [AIR 2014 SC 187]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He also contended that the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Geeta Mehrotra and another vs. State of U.P. and another [(2012) 10 SCC 741] has noticed the casual way in which the cases under Section 498A of IPC are registered and also that parties to a matrimonial dispute unnecessarily implicate all the members of the family.

entities.text: Geeta Mehrotra and another vs. State of U.P. and another [(2012) 10 SCC 741]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He therefore, submitted that in the present case too, petitioner Nos.2, 3 and 4, who were father- in-law, mother-in-law and sister-in-law of respondent No.2 have been unnecessarily implicated in the case.
He further submitted that a Co-ordinate Bench of this Court in similar circumstances in Faisal Ahmed Khan vs. The State of Karnataka and another [ILR 2020 KAR 130] had held

entities.text: Faisal Ahmed Khan vs. The State of Karnataka and another [ILR 2020 KAR 130]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: as follows:-

"20. It is relevant to note that though the complaint contains the allegations recorded above, there is interpolation with regard to the date 03.08.2011, on which date she was allegedly confined in a room and attempt was made to kill her by pouring kerosene.
Further, it is stated that Faizal made an attempt to hang her to a Ceiling fan.
In the NC: 2023:KHC:41424 following sentence, it is stated that Faizal made her fall from a motor cycle and tried to kill her.
The two allegations that Faizal attempted to hang the complainant and thereafter made her fall from the motor cycle contradict each other.
If Faizal had really attempted to hang her, how did she escape from his clutches?
No details are forthcoming in this behalf.

However, even if it is assumed Mr Mirza Haroon Baig vs State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60408745/
3 that the said allegation were true, it is not understandable why she sat on Faisal's motor cycle.

entities.text: Mirza Haroon Baig vs State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 22. Thus, the Complaint is full of unbelievable and self contradicting allegations.
The first allegation of demand for Rs.3,00,000/- is said to have been made jointly by petitioner and his family members.
The second allegation regarding demand of money to purchase a car is alleged jointly against petitioner and his sisters.
Thus all allegations in the complaint are omnibus in nature and in the least, made jointly with other accused and there are no specific against the petitioner."

5. The learned counsel contended that in the present case too, the allegations contained in the complaint lodged by respondent No.2 are perse contradictory and therefore, respondent No.1 ought to have conducted preliminary enquiry to ascertain the truth.

Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 submitted that respondent No.2 was given in marriage on 02.04.2021 and after 15 days, she was sent back to her parents house on the ground that she was obese.
Though a panchayath was held at Gulbarga on 08.08.2021 and respondent No.2 was brought back to Bengaluru, she was locked up in a room and was given very limited food.
She also contends that respondent No.2 who expected a blissful life, suffered mentally at the hands of the petitioners and therefore, the petitioners are to be involved in an investigation.
She submitted that the jurisdictional police are bound to conduct an enquiry before proceeding to file a charge-sheet against the petitioners.
She therefore, submits that it is too premature to hold that the petitioners are innocent of the allegations made and therefore, prayed that the petition be dismissed.
7. The learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 submits that the case is still at premature stage and therefore, innocence of the petitioners cannot be presumed, on their mere say.

I have considered the submissions made by the learned counsel for the petitioners and the learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent No.1 as well as the learned counsel for respondent No.2.
9.
The fact that respondent No.2 was given in marriage to petitioner No.1 on 02.04.2021 is not much in dispute.
The respondent No.2 has claimed that within 15 days of the marriage, her in-laws chided her for being obese and that her parents had deceived them in marrying her off to petitioner No.1.
It also discloses that respondent No.2 was packed off to her parents house within a month from the date of the marriage.
From May 2021 till August 2021, the petitioners did not make any efforts to bring respondent No.2 to matrimonial home.
However, respondent No.2 alleges that a panchayath was held at Gulbarga on 08.08.2021 and she was brought back to matrimonial home only on 09.08.2021.

At Bengaluru, she was locked up in a room and was given food as per the choice of the Mr Mirza Haroon Baig vs State Of Karnataka on 18 November, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60408745/
4 petitioners.

entities.text: Mr Mirza Haroon Baig vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The complaint also discloses that respondent No.2 lived under the constant threat of being divorced by petitioner No.1.
Therefore, it cannot be held that there is no case warranting investigation by respondent No.1.

Further, even after thorough consideration of the complaint lodged by respondent No.2, except a stray allegation that petitioner No.4 joined petitioner Nos.1 to 3, there is no material to indicate that petitioner No.4 had ever abused/ill-treated the respondent No.2, which could constitute an offence under Section 498A of IPC.
In that view of the matter, the petitioner Nos.1 to 3 are bound to be involved in the investigation by the respondent No.1.

The contention of the learned counsel for the petitioners that in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Lalitha Kumari, supra, preliminary investigation must be conducted by respondent No.1 before registering First Information Report, is though indisputable, however, as the offence alleged against the petitioners were cognizable in nature, respondent No.1 was bound to register the First Information Report.

In so far as reliance placed by the learned counsel for the petitioners on the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Geeta Mehrotra, supra, that was a case where the charge-sheet was filed and cognizance was taken by the Magistrate.

In that view of the matter,
petitioners Nos.1 to 3 are bound to cooperate in the investigation by respondent No.1.
- 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:41424 10.

In so far as petitioner No.4 is concerned, since there is no incriminating circumstances warranting respondent No.1 to involve her in the investigation, the registration of First Information Report against her in Crime No.193/2021 by respondent No.1 is liable to be quashed.
11. Consequently, this petition is allowed in part.

The registration of First Information Report against petitioner No.4/accused No.4 in Crime No.193/2021 by respondent No.1 for the offence punishable under Section 498A read with Section 34 of IPC is quashed.
12. The investigation as against other accused shall continue.
It is needless to mention that the investigating officer shall also hear the accused before taking any decision to file a charge-sheet.
